message_test.variant_check: all 4 lines are one idea each, 18 to 29 characters, title case; M1 carries numbers and the others don't, which is the idea itself (proof), so it stays
survey_script: Screener: Do you own your home, and does it have central air conditioning? (yes / no; 'no' ends the survey)
Five-second test: one line, assigned at random and balanced across the 4, shown for 5 seconds. Then: In a few words, what does this company promise?
Preference: all 4 lines in a rotated order. Which of these would make you most likely to book an AC repair? (one answer)
Why that one? (optional, not asked in this run)

audience.why_whole_segment: your own list costs nothing to invite, and the five-second test gains from every extra answer
invitation: We're rewriting our website and want a homeowner's view. 3 questions, under a minute.
There are no right answers: pick what you'd really respond to.

readout.verdict: Decided: M1 beats every other message
readout.caveat: A survey measures what people say they'd respond to, not what they do.

message_test.decision: Lead the AC page hero and the AC Repair ads with M1 "Rated 4.9 by 1,200+ Neighbors". It is clear on the five-second test (81.1% got it).
message_test.next_test: A live split of the final 2 doesn't fit (187 days at this ad group's volume). The paused challenger ad from Mode 1 already carries M1 as a headline: turn it on once you approve it, and read it after 3 weeks or 1,000 impressions per new line. That read is observational, not a controlled test.
